title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 186
paragraphs: This same queen also contrived a trick of the following kind. Over that gate of the city through which the greatest number of people passed, she set up for herself a tomb above the very gate itself. On the tomb she engraved writing which said this: “If any of the kings of Babylon who come after me shall be in want of wealth, let him open my tomb and take as much as he desires; but let him not open it for any other cause, if he is not in want; for that will not be well.” This tomb was undisturbed until the kingdom came to Dareios. But to Dareios it seemed a monstrous thing not to make any use of this gate, and also, when there was money lying there, not to take it, considering that the money itself invited him to do so. Now the reason he would not make any use of this gate was because the corpse would have been above his head as he drove through. He then, I say, opened the tomb and found not indeed money, but the corpse, with writing which said this: “If you had not been insatiable of wealth and basely covetous, you would not have opened the resting-places of the dead.”
